🐛 Describe the bug
After #97506, we now use the test time to compute the number of shards required to run the test and to set the shard timeout value.  One flaky edge case that I'm seeing with the current implementation is in the way it handle slow tests, for example in inductor/test_minifier on ASAN https://hud.pytorch.org/pytorch/pytorch/commit/73b06a0268bb89c09a86f16fa0f72818baa4b250.  Here is what happens:

Lots of tests from inductor/test_minifier were slow https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/blob/b4f5e45cf2602402ea0585c2dc94c7f5dfd525fe/stats/slow-tests.json.  As we use the average test time to detect slow tests, their values were around 60+ to 70+ seconds.
In the latest stats commit today, these tests are not slow anymore pytorch/test-infra@62aa0c4.  So they start to run everywhere.
Tests running on ASAN are generally slower than their non-ASAN equivalent.  Thus, inductor/test_minifier started to timeout there once they ran, i.e. https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/actions/runs/4601886643/jobs/8130489532

There seem to be several questions/issues here:

Are we calculate the number of shards correctly when these slow tests are re-enabled?  I see only 1 shard for inductor/test_minifier before and after.  Thus the latter timed out.
Is using the average test time to detect slow tests the best way to do so?  Take an example, the average time for test_after_aot_cpu_accuracy_error (__main__.MinifierTests) was 74s while its actual test time on ASAN was actually around 250s.  The gap was too big.  It looks like we need the test time per job here.
Is fixing the shard timeout at 30m the way forward because of its simplicity?

I'll go ahead and disable this test on ASAN first to mitigate the issue.  It looks like the majority of the tests are skipped already:

nodes.bodyText:
🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Unable to export to ONNX a model that uses the operation 'aten::unflatten'.
Alternatives
I have tried adding the operation to symbolic_opsetxx.py as per this guide, but as per this issue it seems this wouldn't suffice (it will produce a ONNX model file but it won't work).
Additional context
So, in issue #97262  we got to use a script to register "aten::scaled_dot_product_attention" as a custom operation.
Will need to do the same for "aten::unflatten" until it's supported in an upcoming opset version.
Here's the full script (minus the symbolic_opset18.py changes):
import onnxscript
import torch

# Assuming you use opset18
from onnxscript.onnx_opset import opset18 as op

custom_opset = onnxscript.values.Opset(domain="torch.onnx", version=18)


@onnxscript.script(custom_opset)
def ScaledDotProductAttention(
    query,
    key,
    value,
    dropout_p,
):
    # Swap the last two axes of key
    key_shape = op.Shape(key)
    key_last_dim = key_shape[-1:]
    key_second_last_dim = key_shape[-2:-1]
    key_first_dims = key_shape[:-2]
    # Contract the dimensions that are not the last two so we can transpose
    # with a static permutation.
    key_squeezed_shape = op.Concat(
        op.Constant(value_ints=[-1]), key_second_last_dim, key_last_dim, axis=0
    )
    key_squeezed = op.Reshape(key, key_squeezed_shape)
    key_squeezed_transposed = op.Transpose(key_squeezed, perm=[0, 2, 1])
    key_transposed_shape = op.Concat(key_first_dims, key_last_dim, key_second_last_dim, axis=0)
    key_transposed = op.Reshape(key_squeezed_transposed, key_transposed_shape)

    embedding_size = op.CastLike(op.Shape(query)[-1], query)
    scale = op.Div(1.0, op.Sqrt(embedding_size))

    # Scale q, k before matmul for stability see https://tinyurl.com/sudb9s96 for math
    query_scaled = op.Mul(query, op.Sqrt(scale))
    key_transposed_scaled = op.Mul(key_transposed, op.Sqrt(scale))
    attn_weight = op.Softmax(
        op.MatMul(query_scaled, key_transposed_scaled),
        axis=-1,
    )
    attn_weight, _ = op.Dropout(attn_weight, dropout_p)
    return op.MatMul(attn_weight, value)


def custom_scaled_dot_product_attention(g, query, key, value, attn_mask, dropout, is_causal, scale=None):
    return g.onnxscript_op(ScaledDotProductAttention, query, key, value, dropout).setType(query.type())

torch.onnx.register_custom_op_symbolic(
    symbolic_name="aten::scaled_dot_product_attention",
    symbolic_fn=custom_scaled_dot_product_attention,
    opset_version=18,
)

# Custom operation registered, we can produce our onnx model

from dp.model.model import load_checkpoint
from dp.phonemizer import Phonemizer
from dp.preprocessing.text import Preprocessor

model, checkpoint = load_checkpoint('latin_ipa_forward.pt')

dummy_input = {"batch": {"text":torch.rand((32,32)).long()}}

torch.onnx.export(
    model,                      # PyTorch Model
    dummy_input,                # Input tensor
    "latin_ipa_forward.onnx",   # Output file (eg. 'output_model.onnx')
    custom_opsets = {"torch.onnx": 18},           
    opset_version=18,           # Operator support version
    input_names=['embedding'],  # Input tensor name (arbitary)
    output_names=['fc_out']     # Output tensor name (arbitary)
)

python script:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
    
def conv3x3(in_planes, out_planes, stride=1):
    "3x3 convolution with padding"
    return nn.Conv2d(in_planes, out_planes, kernel_size=3, stride=stride,
                     padding=1, bias=False)

class ChannelAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_planes, ratio=16):
        super(ChannelAttention, self).__init__()
        self.avg_pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d([1, 1])
        self.max_pool = nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d([1, 1])
           
        self.fc = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(in_planes, in_planes // 16, 1, bias=False),
                               nn.ReLU(),
                               nn.Conv2d(in_planes // 16, in_planes, 1, bias=False))
        self.sigmoid = nn.Sigmoid()

    def forward(self, x):
        avg_out = self.fc(self.avg_pool(x))
        max_out = self.fc(self.max_pool(x))
        out = avg_out + max_out
        return self.sigmoid(out)

class SpatialAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, kernel_size=7):
        super(SpatialAttention, self).__init__()

        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(2, 1, kernel_size, padding=kernel_size//2, bias=False)
        self.sigmoid = nn.Sigmoid()

    def forward(self, x):
        avg_out = torch.mean(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)
        max_out, _ = torch.max(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)
        x = torch.cat([avg_out, max_out], dim=1)
        x = self.conv1(x)
        return self.sigmoid(x)

class CBAM(nn.Module):
    expansion = 1

    def __init__(self, inplanes, planes, stride=1, downsample=None):
        super(CBAM, self).__init__()
        self.conv1 = conv3x3(inplanes, planes, stride)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(planes)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        self.conv2 = conv3x3(planes, planes)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(planes)

        self.ca = ChannelAttention(planes)
        self.sa = SpatialAttention()

        self.downsample = downsample
        self.stride = stride

    def forward(self, x):
        residual = x

        out = self.conv1(x)
        out = self.bn1(out)
        out = self.relu(out)

        out = self.conv2(out)
        out = self.bn2(out)

        out = self.ca(out) * out
        out = self.sa(out) * out

        if self.downsample is not None:
            residual = self.downsample(x)

        out += residual
        out = self.relu(out)

        return out

if __name__ == '__main__':
    model = CBAM(16, 16)
    device = 'cuda:0'
    model.to(device)
    model.eval()
    dummpy_input = torch.zeros([1, 16, 400, 640], device=device)
    torch.onnx.export(
        model, 
        dummpy_input, 
        'model.onnx', 
        verbose=True,
        input_names=["input"],
        output_names=["output"],
        opset_version=14,
    )

    @onlyNativeDeviceTypes
    @dtypes(torch.int64, torch.float32, torch.complex64)
    def test_copy_transpose_math_view(self, device, dtype):
        src = make_tensor((100, 100), dtype=dtype, device=device).transpose(0, 1)
        dst = torch.empty((100, 100), dtype=dtype, device=device)

        dst._neg_view().copy_(src)
        self.assertEqual(dst, -src)
        dst._neg_view().copy_(src._neg_view())
        self.assertEqual(dst, src)
        dst.copy_(src._neg_view())
        self.assertEqual(dst, -src)

        if dtype.is_complex:
            dst.conj().copy_(src)
            self.assertEqual(dst, src.conj_physical())
            dst.conj().copy_(src.conj())
            self.assertEqual(dst, src)
            dst.copy_(src.conj())
            self.assertEqual(dst, src.conj_physical())

nodes.bodyText:
🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Many models feature residual blocks, aka skip connections, where some computation is done, and then the original tensor is added to the result at the end of the block.
Also common are models where the same input is processed in two independent ways, before being summed. Residual blocks can be seen as a special case of this, where one branch is nn.Identity.
I think having a built in module for either of these setups would be very convenient. ResNet, in torchvision, for example would no longer need custom modules for BasicBlock or Bottleneck. The readability would be higher too.
I would propose syntax like:
nn.Residual(
  nn.Sequential(...)
)

nn.ParallelSum(
  module1,
  module2
)
Alternatives
The alternative currently is to write a custom module. While it's not much code, it is 90% boilerplate, and I think there is some clarity in having named operations for residuals.
There was a proposal for nn.Parallel which is somewhat similar to this, but it was rejected as too niche.
I searched the issues, and couldn't find this suggestion put forward before.
Additional context
I believe this would be fairly straightforward to implement and am happy to put together a PR if this feature is desired.
cc @albanD @mruberry @jbschlosser @walterddr @mikaylagawarecki

nodes.title: Compiling complex-valued functions fails

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
Within at::native::countRadixUsingMask, the __activemask intrinsic is used to conduct a warp vote (__ballot_sync(__activemask(), vote)) between the threads counting the distribution of the radix within the input data.
Since at least CUDA 9, __activemask should not be used to determine which threads are along the same execution path as detailed in this NVIDIA blog post. Since there is not a guarantee all threads within the same execution path are in the same active thread group, the distribution count results can be off resulting in an wrong assumption of unique results in at::native::findPattern which leads to a data race. Can affect topk, kthvalue, and median operators since all three rely on at::native::radixSelect.
The issue is hard to reproduce since even though CUDA does not guarantee threads in the same execution path operate within the same active thread group, in practice, this divergence is rare.
Example crash when using topk
import torch
x = torch.tensor([0, 1, 2]).cuda()
x.topk(1)
aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorTopK.cu:144:gatherTopK: assertion: outputSliceSize >= writeIndexStar

Versions
Affects all versions since at least #17544
cc @ngimel

    # ✔️ torch.relu, torch.add(_, 1)

ret_eager = fn(x)
compiled = torch.compile(fn)
ret_compiled = compiled(x)

🐛 Describe the bug
The following program produces inconsistent results in eager mode and compile mode, and according to the semantics of each operator, result from torch.compile is incorrect. Note that unfold() and abs_ are necessary for triggering the issue while torch.add can be replaced by any other operator.
import torch

def fn(x):
    # x: (1, 5)
    t1 = torch.add(x, x)
    t2 = t1.unfold(1, 3, 2) # t2: (1, 2, 3)
    t3 = t2.abs_()
    return t3

x = torch.rand([1, 5])
ret_eager = fn(x)
compiled = torch.compile(fn)
ret_compiled = compiled(x)

assert torch.allclose(
    ret_eager, ret_compiled,
    rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-3, equal_nan=True,
), '\n'.join([
    '',
    f'>>> ret_eager',
    str(ret_eager),
    f'>>> ret_compiled',
    str(ret_compiled),
])
print('==== Check OK! ====')

"""

🐛 Describe the bug
The shape function for transposed convolution defined here  https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/jit/_shape_functions.py#L805
if transposed:
            kernel = dilation_ * (weight[d] - 1)
            output_size.append((input[d] - 1) * stride[d - 2] - 2 * padding[d - 2] + kernel + 1)

does not include output_padding, whereas the shape function for this op, as defined by the documentation here https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.ConvTranspose2d.html#torch.nn.ConvTranspose2d, includes output_padding. That looks like a bug.
Versions
This was observed while using the latest TorchMLIR, which in turn refers to these shape functions.

🐛 Describe the bug
bug
Project can't link against googletest along with pytorch.
What I have is a trivial example using googletest
# CMakeLists.txt
add_executable(testt ./main.cpp)
set_property(TARGET testt PROPERTY CXX_STANDARD 17)
target_link_libraries(testt PRIVATE gtest_main)
# commenting out ${TORCH_LIBRARIES} linking seems to get it to work
target_link_libraries(testt PRIVATE ${TORCH_LIBRARIES})

root@c4464de3e772:/workspace/pytorch_gtest_repro/build# make
[ 20%] Built target gtest
[ 40%] Built target gtest_main
[ 50%] Linking CXX executable testt
/usr/bin/ld: CMakeFiles/testt.dir/main.cpp.o: in function `add_negative_flag(std::string const&)':
main.cpp:(.text+0x2b): undefined reference to `testing::FLAGS_gtest_filter'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
make[2]: *** [CMakeFiles/testt.dir/build.make:114: testt] Error 1
make[1]: *** [CMakeFiles/Makefile2:137: CMakeFiles/testt.dir/all] Error 2
make: *** [Makefile:136: all] Error 2

background
Note1: This only repros with pip package from upstream. If I switch the system to use my locally built pytorch pip wheel, it actually compiles fine. So I'm pretty convinced that there's something wrong with upstream pip package.
Note2: In my desperate debugging, peeking into the binaries
root@e09e5ed6d13a:/workspace/pytorch_gtest_repro/build# nm /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/lib*.so | grep -i FLAGS_ | grep gflags
000000000001f560 t _GLOBAL__sub_I_flags_use_no_gflags.cpp

00000000000254b0 t _GLOBAL__sub_I_flags_use_no_gflags.cpp

Looks like neither upstream pip wheel nor my local pip build uses gflags.
The real error also expands to more than just the FLAGS_gtest_filter on my full project, so I don't think it's a gflag only problem.

🐛 Describe the bug
Bug
I launched training of this repo with torch.distributed.launch and it worked well. On top of the code in the repo, I tried to let every GPU print training logs to different files by adding the following code:
if args.rank == args.test_env:
    args.out_file = os.path.join(args.experiment_path, "log_main.txt")
    args.out_file = open(args.out_file, "w")
    log_str = print_args(args)
    print_log(log_str, args)
else:
    args.out_file = os.path.join(args.experiment_path, f"log_rank{args.rank}.txt")
    args.out_file = open(args.out_file, "w")

The strange thing is, sometimes it worked well, but sometimes one of the nodes beside the test_env node (rank==0) would report error FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '../experiment_results/FedSR/OfficeHome/3/20230329_210405-FedSR_reproduction/log_rank2.txt'. The rank of the node that report the error differs when I run the training script multiple times.
To Reproduce
Clone this repo and create src/test.py:
import os 
import random
import sys 
import importlib
from tqdm import tqdm
from collections import defaultdict, OrderedDict
from datetime import datetime
import subprocess

import torch

from datasets import *

from prepare import *

args.experiment_path = os.path.join(args.experiment_path, args.method, args.dataset, str(args.test_env), args.experiment_name)
if args.rank == args.test_env and not os.path.exists(args.experiment_path):
    os.system("mkdir -p " + args.experiment_path)
if args.rank == args.test_env:

    args.out_file = open(args.out_file, "w")
    log_str = print_args(args)

else:
    args.out_file = os.path.join(args.experiment_path, f"log_rank{args.rank}.txt")
    args.out_file = open(args.out_file, "w")

Then, create and run test.sh:
cd src


# Office-Home
currenttime=`date "+%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"`
method="FedSR"
seed=0
data_dir="../data/"
experiment_path="../experiment_results/"

# OfficeHome
for test_env in 0 1 2 3
do
experiment_name=${currenttime}"-FedSR"
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$1 python -m torch.distributed.launch --nproc_per_node=4 --master_port $RANDOM -m \
    test --dataset OfficeHome --test_env ${test_env} --method ${method} --total_iters 5000 --optim SGD \
    --back_bone resnet50 --train_split 0.9 --z_dim 2048 --L2R_coeff 0.05 --CMI_coeff 0.0005 \
    --num_samples 20 --seed ${seed} --rounds_per_eval 10 --E 5 --batchsize 64 --lr 0.01 \
    --weight_decay 0.0005 --dataset_folder ${data_dir} --experiment_path ${experiment_path} \
    --experiment_name ${experiment_name} --save_checkpoint False --distributed True --world_size 4
done

nodes.title: torch.distributed.launch: Possible error when writing to different files from different nodes.

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
The following program works fine in eager mode but triggers a compilation error when using torch.compile. Some details for debugging are illustrated in the comments (✔️ means that the program terminates without error, ❌ means that compilation error occurs).
It's probably related to #94055.
import torch

def fn(x, y):
    t = torch.bitwise_and(x, y) # ✔️ works fine w/o this line
    return torch.clamp_max(t, y)
    # ❌ return torch.max(t, y)

x = torch.rand([5, 10, 1]).to(torch.int8)
y = torch.rand([10, 1]).to(torch.int8)

# ✔️ x, y are cuda tensors

# ❌ torch.bool, torch.int8, torch.int16, torch.uint8, torch.uint16
# ✔️ torch.int32, torch.int64

ret_eager = fn(x, y)
print('==== Eager mode OK! ====')

compiled = torch.compile(fn)
print('==== torchcomp compilation OK! ====')

ret_compiled = compiled(x, y)
print('==== torchcomp mode OK! ====')

nodes.bodyText:
🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Please consider my toy model, which has a softmax which is independent of any input:
import torch

class MyModel(torch.nn.Module):

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.vec = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(10, 1000))


    def forward(self, x):
        # Does not depend on input, Can be precomputed.
        norm = torch.softmax(self.vec, -1)

        # Depends on input, cannot be precomputed.
        return x + norm


model = MyModel()
with torch.no_grad():
    torch.onnx.export(model, (torch.randn(10, 1000),), 'const-fold.onnx',
        input_names=['input'],
        output_names=['output'],
        do_constant_folding=True,
    )
However, even with do_constant_folding=True, the softmax node does not get folded:

Softmax preserves tensor volume so folding it shouldn't bloat the produced ONNX file.
It seems like this would be a matter of adding Softmax to this giant if/else block.
Maybe there are also some other ops which constant folding could be supported for. Matmul would be nice but it has the potential to produce huge tensors in the exported ONNX model.
Thanks!
Alternatives
No response

nodes.bodyText:
🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Rotary embeddings are becoming more and more popular. It would be nice if PyTorch supported them directly, instead of having to refer to research libraries.
Rotary embeddings require performing transformations to key and query matrices as described in the following paper:
https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09864
An example implementation can be found in the xFormers library. Due to the fact that these transformations are applied to the key and query matrices (i.e. after the projections) and not the hidden states, it would need to be added as an option for F.multi_head_attention.
Alternatives
No response
Additional context
No response

nodes.bodyText:
🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
It would be nice to have a simple way to convert between float and complex types of the same precision. Something like
dtype = torch.float32
print(dtype.to_complex())
# torch.complex64

dtype = torch.complex128
print(dtype.to_float())
# torch.float64

dtype = torch.float64
print(dtype.to_float())
# torch.float64
Alternatives

building a dictionnary that stores conversions from float to complex types of the same precision
using this unpleasant/difficult to read workaround: getattr(torch, torch.finfo(dtype).dtype)

Additional context
We are building a library for the simulation of quantum systems built on torch (see torchqdynamics), and conversion between float and complex types happens all the time. Quantum objects are always complex, but time is always float-like, and it's essential that they are of the same precision.
cc @ezyang @anjali411 @dylanbespalko @mruberry @lezcano @nikitaved

I believe what is happening here is:

Thread 1 is attempting to allocate memory through the DeviceCachingAllocator, which (when memory history recording is enabled) eventually calls back into the GIL to release the recorded back-trace for an allocation. Thread 1 blocks on the GIL, which thread 553 holds.
Thread 553 is also attempting to call into the DeviceCachingAllocator while holding the GIL (since THPStorage_resize_ calls into the allocator but does NOT free the GIL). Since thread 1 holds the DeviceCachingAllocator, Thread 553 blocks waiting for Thread 1 to release it

It may be that we need to enforce that all callers of the CachingAllocator must release the GIL

🐛 Describe the bug
Pattern replacement behaves incorrectly when the replacement pattern maps inputs to outputs - such a pattern can be used to replace redundant code. However, current code in torch.fx.subgraph_rewriter._replace_pattern causes the list of replacement nodes to include the entire graph before that node, resulting in an exponential slowdown due to recursive calls traversing the entire graph multiple times. This slowdown is trivial in the example code but very significant in production models.
To reproduce:
import torch
from torch.fx.subgraph_rewriter import replace_pattern_with_filters
from torch.fx.experimental.proxy_tensor import make_fx

def model(x):
    x = (x+2) - 3 + x.T
    return x.unsqueeze(0).squeeze()

def redundant_pattern(input):
    x = torch.ops.aten.unsqueeze.default(input, 0)
    return torch.ops.aten.squeeze.default(x)
def replacement(input):
    return input

x = torch.randn(2,2)
gm = make_fx(model)(x)
gm.graph.print_tabular()
matches = replace_pattern_with_filters(gm, redundant_pattern, replacement, [])
print(matches[0].replacements)  # Expected only [add_2], instead see all parents of add_2
My proposed fix is to add a check in _replace_pattern to prevent the call to get_replacement_nodes:
        for ret_node in copied_returning_nodes:
            if ret_node in match.placeholder_nodes:
                replacement_nodes.append(ret_node)
            else:
                get_replacement_nodes(ret_node)

The FSDP implementation resides in torch/distributed/fsdp/, where different logical functionalities are separated into their respective files. This separation was done as part of a refactoring effort last year. Overview
The purpose of this task is to merge _utils.py into _common_utils.py and adjust any imports accordingly. This should help ramp up the development workflow and provide some initial familiarity with the code base.

🐛 Describe the bug
Hi! This is a bug found by a fuzzer which might be uncommon in the real world. However, it looks like an unseen internal error.  So I still report it in case it might lead to other problems.
import torch
